dedupe_keys.name: modelled yield and production losses from ground level ozone for maize rice soybean and wheat 2010 2012 ukceh eidc

description: Two global 1 by 1 degree gridded datasets of modelled crop losses caused by ground-level ozone pollution for maize, rice, soybean and wheat, averaged over 2010 to 2012: percentage yield loss (version 2) and production loss in thousand tonnes per cell. The DataCite records, from the NERC Environmental Information Data Centre, say losses were placed using the FAO GAEZ crop production distribution for 2000, with ozone from the EMEP MSC-W chemical transport model (version 4.16), to identify areas at high ozone risk. Both were published in July 2020 by K. Sharps, G. Mills, D. Simpson, H. Pleijel, M. Frei, K. Burkey, L. Emberson, J. Uddling, M. Broberg, Z. Feng, K. Kobayashi and M. Agrawal as downloadable shapefiles, free under the Open Government Licence v3.0; the catalogue page lists copyright holders including UKCEH, the Norwegian Meteorological Institute, the University of Gothenburg, the University of Bonn, the USDA and SEI York. They support a 2018 Global Change Biology paper. Caveats: crop distribution is for 2000 and the dose-response relationships carry model uncertainty. For simulation it gives an air-quality stress on staple crop yields, to combine with climate and drought impacts in food supply models. Related catalogue records include FAO-IIASA GAEZ and the GGCMI crop model outputs.
